持.meaning: A sailor leaves his <part>anchor</part> at the <part>temple</part> and asks a monk to mind it. The monk grips it in both arms all day, through prayers and lunch, never once setting it down. All he can do is <kanji>hold</kanji>.
持.on: At sunset the sailor rattles back in a muddy <sound>jee</sound>p, and the monk drops the anchor in the back.
持.kun: A <sound>mo</sound>ccasin slips off the monk's foot, dust tickles his nose, and he sneezes: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' Still he doesn't let go.

降.meaning: A climber plants her <part>pennant</part> on the summit, then unfolds a <part>folding chair</part> and rides it like a sled down a stone <part>staircase</part>, bump, bump, bump, all the way to the bottom. That's one way to <kanji>descend</kanji>.
降.on: At the bottom she's still clutching the ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne she bought at the top, now flat as a pancake.
降.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' she yelps at every bump on the way down the stairs.

免.meaning: A kid sneaks out of class with a scarf <part>wrap</part>ped round his head, his <part>mouth</part> full of reasons and his <part>legs</part> already running. 'Dentist! Grandma! Dog ate my shoes!' The teacher just sighs at one more <kanji>excuse</kanji>.
免.on: He scribbled his excuse on the back of a café <sound>me</sound>nu, and the teacher reads it and gets hungry.
免.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, the <sound>noo</sound>k!' he whispers, and hides in a reading nook behind a bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic. Nobody finds him: he escapes.

晩.meaning: The <part>sun</part> sinks low, and a <part>rabbit</part> hops out of its burrow, ears up, nose twitching. It has waited all day for this: the sky going orange, then purple, then dark. Rabbit time is <kanji>nightfall</kanji>.
晩.on: The rabbit drags a sticky <sound>bun</sound> out of its burrow and nibbles it under the first stars.

飯.meaning: A plate of <part>food</part> sits in front of a kid who is firmly <part>anti</part> broccoli: arms crossed, mouth shut. Mum stands guard. Nobody leaves the table until it's eaten. It's the longest <kanji>meal</kanji> of the year.
飯.on: In the end Mum gives in and pours <sound>hon</sound>ey all over the broccoli.
飯.kun: Then a <sound>me</sound>ssy <sound>shee</sound>p wanders in from the garden and gobbles the broccoli off the plate.
